buy_title: If you want a warm bed for pennies a night, order this one
buy_total: The button is a paid link: as an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases, and it never changes what you pay. Prices in this guide come from other US stores and the makers' sites in November 2026 and move with sales; the button shows today's price.
buy_kicker: Our first pick, and our last word

cards.name: Sunbeam Restful Quilted Heated Mattress Pad, Queen (dual controllers)
cards.badge: Our first pick · the cheapest warm bed
cards.price: About $60 at Walmart in a search listing seen Nov 9, 2026 (list $79.87); Wi-Fi versions from about $78
cards.buy_if: you sleep cold, your bedroom is the only cold room, and you want to turn the heat down a few degrees for the night: a pad runs for pennies, not dollars.
cards.skip_if: you need to warm a whole room (a pad heats the bed, not the air), or you want a product with no controller-failure history: owners of several brands report controllers quitting within a season or two.
cards.owners: Sunbeam's own manual (read Nov 9, 2026) lists a 10-hour auto-off and a 3-year limited warranty; retail listings say 5 years, so read the one in your box. The common complaint at Target and in blanket-review round-ups is a controller that fails after the warranty.

buy.pick: Queen size, dual controllers (one per side), the Restful quilted pad; the Wi-Fi version costs about $18 more and adds nothing to the cost per night.
buy.check: Sold by Sunbeam or a major retailer, a UL or ETL mark on the controller label, and the model number on the label (we found no recall for the Restful pads; the 2023 Sunbeam recall was a different queen blanket, model 32810027).
buy.label: See today's price

cards.name: Sunbeam Microplush Heated Blanket, Queen (BSM9KQS)
cards.badge: The same pennies, on top of you
cards.price: No store price confirmed in November 2026; heated blankets run about $50 to $130 at major retailers
cards.buy_if: you want the heat on top of you, you wash it often, or you already have a mattress pad you like.
cards.skip_if: you share a bed and fight over the controls (a pad has one control per side, a queen blanket usually too, but check), or you want a wattage on the box before buying: Sunbeam does not print one on the pages we could reach.
cards.owners: A 10-hour auto-off and two digital controllers per the manual summary we read (Nov 9, 2026). We found no owner counts at stores other than Amazon for this model, so we make no claim about how it holds up.
cards.cta_label: Check the Sunbeam queen blanket on Amazon

cards.name: Dreo Atom One 1500W ceramic heater (DR-HSH004)
cards.badge: The room heater that costs about $2 a night
cards.buy_if: you want to warm one small room before bed or while you work, with a thermostat and a timer.
cards.skip_if: you plan to sleep with it running (Consumer Reports says turn a heater off when you go to bed), or you own the recalled Dreo DR-HSH015 model (see the recall box).
cards.owners: Dreo.com's Trustpilot page (read Oct 15, 2026) shows fast warm-up and one reviewer who lost output after five to six weeks. See our Dreo review for the full read.
cards.cta_label: Check the Dreo Atom One on Amazon

cards.name: Pelonis HO-0279 1,500 W oil-filled radiator
cards.badge: Slow to warm, quiet, holds heat
cards.price: About $60 and up at Home Depot (a Slickdeals commenter, January 2026); one Walmart listing near $118 (undated)
cards.buy_if: you want quiet, steady background heat in a bedroom for an evening and don't mind the wait for it to warm up.
cards.skip_if: you want heat in the first five minutes (use a ceramic fan heater) or you need a model with a warranty we could read: we could not open Pelonis's page (it returned an error on Nov 9, 2026).
cards.owners: A Home Depot reviewer measured about 600, 860 and 1,400 W on the three settings (seen in a search summary). Others report a unit that failed to turn on after months, and a maker reply.
cards.cta_label: Check the Pelonis oil-filled heater on Amazon
